Source inspiration: [@mathewsSite].

## Description

A Laurent series of a function around a center $x_0$, valid in an annulus $r<|x-x_0|<R$ of the complex plane on which $f$ is analytic, is

$$
f(x)=\sum_{k=-\infty}^{\infty} a_k (x-x_0)^k,
$$

which extends Taylor series by allowing negative powers. Those negative-power terms form the principal part and capture pole-like behavior. When $f$ is analytic at $x_0$, as it is in every case below, its Laurent series on the largest disc $|x-x_0|<R$ on which $f$ is analytic has zero principal part and is the ordinary Taylor series.

## Animations

The Laurent animation for this topic reuses the same 27 function/interval/center cases used on the Padé page, but draws truncated series about $x_0$ instead of rational Padé forms.

All 27 functions are analytic at $x_0$, so on the largest disc about $x_0$ on which $f$ is analytic, $a_k=0$ for every $k<0$, and the two-sided truncation

$$
\sum_{k=-N}^{N} a_k (x-x_0)^k=\sum_{k=0}^{N} a_k (x-x_0)^k
$$

is the degree-$N$ Taylor polynomial. That is what each frame draws, with $N$ increasing frame by frame; no frame contains a negative power. Unless $f$ is entire (cases 08–11, 13–15 and 18–21), the series converges only within the distance from $x_0$ to the nearest singularity of $f$ in the complex plane and diverges beyond it, and every such plotted interval reaches past that distance. Case 03's window passes that distance only on $10<x\le 10.5$, and case 06's on $4<x\le 4.1$ and $-0.5\le x<0$. On $10<x\le 10.5$ (case 03) and $4<x\le 4.1$ (case 06) the ten frames do not show the divergence: the error falls from each frame to the next. At $x=10.5$ in case 03 the error keeps falling until $N=15$, and at $x=4.1$ in case 06 until $N=20$; after that it grows with every further term (checked to $N=80$). In case 06 the divergence shows only for $x<0$, where $\log x$ is not real and no $f$ curve is drawn: there every term after the constant is negative, so the blue curve sinks with each frame and drops below the bottom of the window ($y=-6$) at the left edge in frames 9 and 10 (at $x=-0.5$ the partial sum is $-6.10$ for $N=9$ and $-7.03$ for $N=10$). Where the nearest singularity is a pole ($\tan x$ in case 12, $\Gamma(x)$ in cases 22–24), a different Laurent series about $x_0$, with nonzero negative powers, holds in the annulus between that pole and the next singularity; the animations do not draw it.

Each case below follows the same case ordering as the Padé suite (Case 01 through Case 27).
